steps.note: an eight second screen recording, open in the ORDINARY editor as one clip: one row on the timeline, one bar, nothing cut yet. A grip at each end of the bar, because the clip is picked

the bar's left end dragged inwards by a second. The recording still starts where it started: the frames came off the front and the bar closed up from its far end, so the transport counts to seven and there is no hole at the start to tidy up

THE FIRST TEST: the same edge dragged back out as far as it goes, and all eight seconds are there again. Nothing was destroyed by the trim; it only moved an in point, and the recording behind it never went anywhere

THE SECOND TEST: two cuts and the take is three SHOTS on ONE row, not three rows. The playhead is the cut line, so cutting took no tool and no aim. All three pieces still read the same recording. The second cut left the MIDDLE piece picked, which is the bit between the two cuts and nearly always the bit you were cutting out

one press of Delete and the middle shot is gone. The join CLOSED: everything after it slid back and the recording is six seconds, on the bar, on the ruler and in the transport. There is no hole to tidy up, because a clip's pieces cannot have one

THE THIRD TEST: the last shot picked up and dropped at the front. What plays, what the playhead reads and what an export would write all follow the new order straight away, because a piece's place is never stored anywhere else

the shot in hand at twice speed. It keeps the frames it reads and takes half as long over them, so everything after it moved along and the whole thing got shorter. Its sound goes with it at the same rate, because the sound is part of the piece rather than a separate thing to keep in step. The bar says 2x on the piece it is true of and says nothing on the ones it is not
hold on the frame under the playhead. A freeze is not a special object: it dropped onto the bar as an ordinary piece, marked hold, and it can be moved, lengthened and thrown away like any other piece
THE FOURTH TEST: eight presses of Command Z and the take is one eight second clip again. Every one of those edits was ONE history step, the same as every other edit in the app
